title: Houthis Capture Red Sea Port City of Mocha
detail: Houthi forces seized control of the Yemeni port city of Mocha (al-Makha) on September 10, 2026, after National Resistance Forces commander Tareq Saleh ordered what was described as a 'tactical withdrawal and repositioning' at dawn, letting the city's defenses collapse. Mocha was the last major Red Sea port still fully under the internationally recognized government's control, sitting roughly 75km north of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Its loss cuts supply lines between Mocha and Taiz and raises fears of disrupted Saudi oil-export routes to Asian markets; analysts described it as a potential turning point that could accelerate a broader breakdown of government forces in southern Yemen. Government air forces have since bombed Houthi positions in and around the city and neighboring Dhubab.

media.caption: Mocha, the last major Red Sea port held by Yemen's government, fell to Houthi forces on Sep 10
